title_en: Chinese Humor (20/20): A Blind Date at the Coffee Shop
note_en: An awkward set-up date over coffee, thawed by talk about cats, is just one example of the huge 相亲 ("arranged dating") phenomenon in China. Then comes a collection of viral stories: a man exposed on stage by his own wife, a "veteran" with a spreadsheet of more than two hundred and sixty dates, young people who dress badly on purpose to get turned down, and park "matchmaking corners" where parents advertise their children's details without even asking them.

sentences.en: This kind of awkward set-up date arranged by friends or relatives has long been a cliché among young Chinese people; compared with the "hardcore" approach of the park "matchmaking corners," where parents swap their children's height, salary and property details directly, breaking the ice slowly over cats seems especially gentle.

phrases.en: This kind of awkward set-up date arranged by friends or relatives has long been a cliché among young Chinese people; compared with the "hardcore" approach of the park "matchmaking corners," where parents swap their children's height, salary and property details directly, breaking the ice slowly over cats seems especially gentle.

sentences.en: Big matchmaking events in the style of "Granny Wang the matchmaker" always draw crowds of onlookers: one man in his fifties went on stage claiming to be single and trying to impress two female guests, only for his wife, just back from the toilet, to walk out of the audience and expose him on the spot.

only for his wife, just back from the toilet, to walk out of the audience and expose him on the spot.
